text:
maria: Quick check — after the poetry update my local venv can't stream with the async client, getting `TypeError: 'async_generator' object is not iterable`. anyone seen this?

sam: hm, that sounds like an async iterator vs list bug. which versions are you on? poetry.lock or pip?

maria: poetry.lock. redwood-sdk 0.8.1, httpx 0.24.3, python 3.11. streaming call is `await client.chat.stream(...)` and then `for chunk in stream:` error thrown immediately.

jordan: streaming API changed a bit in 0.8.x — the client returns an async iterator you need `async for chunk in stream:` not a regular `for`. could that be it?

maria: oh wow. that was the main issue for me when running in uvicorn workers it previously worked because I was wrapping with `asyncio.run`. but correct, local tests used `for` accidentally. thanks. :facepalm:

lee: also fwiw, we had a lockfile edge where poetry exported a wheel with an older httpx that returned a sync generator in some edge combos. try `poetry run pip install --upgrade httpx==0.24.4` inside the venv if the `async for` change doesn't fix it.

taylor: small gotcha — if you have both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_TOKEN env vars set, the client prioritizes REDWOOD_API_TOKEN which our docs didn't call out clearly. we had a user whose auth was silently falling back to a stale token in their shell.

maria: good call. i only had REDWOOD_API_KEY in my .env but my system env had REDWOOD_API_TOKEN from an old session (😬). quick repro:

```
# .env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_abc
# exported globally earlier
# REDWOOD_API_TOKEN=pk_live_old
```

shipbot: deploy-bot: published redwood-sdk 0.8.2 with a streaming docs fix and priority-env-doc update. changelog: https://github.com/redwood/repo/releases/tag/0.8.2

jordan: nice. 0.8.2 also pins a compat range for httpx and fixes the `async for` example in the quickstart.

maria: installed 0.8.2, `async for` fixed my local issue and explicit env cleanup fixed auth shadowing. will open a tiny PR to the quickstart and add a note about env var precedence + a line in troubleshooting. pinging @sam for a quick review when available.

sam: can do a fast review tomorrow morning. also recommend adding a lint rule in docs CI to run the snippet with python -m pytest-sphinx or a quick smoke to catch `for` vs `async for` examples.

maria: agreed — i'll add a test under docs/snippets/test_streaming.py that runs the quickstart example in async mode. thanks all! :thumbsup:
